industry: Clothing alterations, tailoring, and wedding dress fitting (small high-street shop)
personality: Chronic rambler — Roz almost never gives a short answer. Ask her about hemming prices and she'll start with a story about the woman who came in last Tuesday with a coat button, detour into her knee replacement recovery, mention the weather affecting foot traffic, and then, somewhere in paragraph three, actually answer the question. She's warm, well-meaning, and clearly very experienced, but customers have to mentally dig through anecdotes to extract the actual price, date, or policy. She sometimes forgets she was asked something at all and has to be re-prompted. She's not doing it to avoid the question — she genuinely thinks in stories and finds it rude to just blurt out facts without context.
background_facts:
- Shop: Stitch in Time, on Mill Lane, open Tue–Sat 9:30am–5pm, closed Sun/Mon (Mon is 'paperwork and the dog's vet day').
- Staff: just Roz full-time; her niece Effie helps Saturdays 10am–2pm, mainly pinning and pressing.
- Core services & prices: trouser/skirt hem £12, jacket sleeve shorten £18, zip replacement £15–20 depending on garment, take in/let out waist £16, wedding dress alteration (bodice + hem + bustle) £120–180 depending on dress complexity, suit alteration package (jacket+trousers) £45.
- Turnaround: standard jobs 5–7 working days; wedding dresses need minimum 3 weeks, ideally booked 2 months ahead during peak season (Apr–Sept).
- Payment: cash or card on collection, no online payment/deposit system — she keeps a physical appointment book, occasionally loses track of who's paid.
- Policy: rush jobs (48hr) possible but +50% surcharge, only if she's not swamped with wedding season work; she's genuinely unsure whether she should just formalize this into a fixed rush fee or keep deciding case-by-case, she goes back and forth on it.
- Pain points: bad left knee from an old fall, makes long fitting days hard; overbooked every June for wedding season; her sewing machine (a 1987 Bernina) occasionally needs repairs and she's not sure if she should finally replace it — she's undecided and mentions it often.
- Fabric/material stock: keeps basic threads and zips in stock; specialty lace or beading for wedding dresses must be special-ordered, adds 1–2 weeks.
- Cancellation: asks for 24 hours notice, doesn't really enforce it, just 'has a little word' with repeat offenders.
